Replicating their experiments on modern hardware would directly test whether the claimed mitigation of computational cost holds in practice, especially for scaling to longer sequences.

[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical analysis of attention complexity scaling (e.g., Tay et al., 2022, 'Efficient Transformers: A Survey') — A systematic survey of sparse attention variants provides a theoretical framework comparing O(n^2) dense attention to O(n log n) or O(n) sparse alternatives. Cross-referencing empirical results with theoretical bounds would help confirm whether the mitigation is substantial and generalizable across transformer-based models.

[PATH:literature] Meta-analysis of sparse attention vs. dense attention on standard NLP benchmarks (e.g., GLUE, SQuAD, long-range arena) — Compiling and statistically analyzing published results from multiple studies (e.g., Reformer, Sparse Transformers, Longformer, BigBird) would reveal whether the efficiency gains consistently translate to competitive performance, thus confirming or refuting the hypothesis that sparse attention enables efficient scaling without significant quality loss.
